clue.text: Fresh air must stun these flowers

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters of these three words are made anew in another order

explanation.surface: A gust of clean air is said to stagger some garden blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like it describes the air, but it signals an anagram of AIR MUST STUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasturtiums are trailing garden plants with bright orange and yellow blooms.

clue.text: Helicon upthrusting to touch it

indicators.note: in a down clue, thrusting upward means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a helicon is a large circular brass instrument of the tuba family, worn round the player's body

explanation.surface: Mount Helicon, home of the Muses, rises up so as to reach something.
explanation.walkthrough: Helicon looks like the Greek mountain, but here it is the coiled brass instrument; 'upthrusting' turns TUBA upward in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to border on or be in contact with something adjacent.

clue.text: In a child right can be wrong

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for right inside the word for a small child

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A remark that, in a youngster's eyes, a right can turn into a wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the start puts R inside TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a tort is a civil wrong, such as negligence, for which damages can be claimed.

clue.text: Old magistrates giving severe punishment

indicators.note: punishment suggests the word severe is knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Historic local officials who were known for handing out harsh penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punishment' signals an anagram of SEVERE; the surface makes it sound like the magistrates' sentencing.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeves were local officials in medieval England, a role akin to a district judge or bailiff.

clue.text: Ordered pink tandoori rice, without egg-amazing Asian speciality

indicators.note: ordered suggests the letters of the restaurant dish are put into a new order

parts.note: an egg is round and stands for the letter O

explanation.surface: A diner orders tandoori with pink rice but no egg, a remarkable Indian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes an O (egg, from its shape) out of PINK TANDOORI RICE before 'Ordered' rearranges what is left. 'Ordered' wants to mean asked for in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian rope trick is a legendary illusion in which a rope rises unsupported and a boy climbs it.

clue.text: Violence for a month on the border

parts.note: May is a month of the year
a hem is the folded border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Fighting breaks out for a whole month along a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem means wild disorder and violent chaos.

clue.text: Give automatic authorisation for masseurs to press down with repeated blows

parts.note: masseurs rub their clients, so they are rubbers
to tamp is to pack something down with repeated light strokes

explanation.surface: Massage therapists work their clients over with a pounding technique.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a massage session; the definition is the bureaucratic sense, approving without scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubber-stamp is to approve a decision routinely, without proper consideration.

clue.text: Led astray around gloomy old English fortification

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters sit on either side of the word for gloomy
astray suggests the letters of led wander into another order

parts.note: an overcast sky is gloomy and grey

explanation.surface: Someone misled about some dark ancient English stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' scrambles the first word to D_LE, and 'around' wraps it round the weather word. Dover Castle is a medieval fortress on the Kent coast, above the white cliffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover Castle is a great medieval stronghold guarding the shortest Channel crossing.

clue.text: Wrestling for a quantity of money gets nothing

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A bout of grappling for a cash prize ends with no reward.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese style of heavyweight ring wrestling.

clue.text: Time for mercy, when all bills should be paid?

definitions.text: when all bills should be paid?

parts.note: to give quarter is to show mercy to a defeated enemy
days, as in 'in my days', means time or era

explanation.surface: A plea for clemency on settling day, when the accounts fall due.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarter days were the four fixed dates each year in England when rents and debts fell due.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarter days were the traditional dates for paying rent and settling accounts each quarter of the year.

clue.text: Sailor going to be a priest

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common term for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman takes holy orders and becomes a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is a French title for a cleric or abbot.

clue.text: Zenith of mountain climb dizzy but not needing medical aid

indicators.note: dizzy suggests the letters of the climb are spun around into a new order

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is the qualification of a doctor who gives medical help

explanation.surface: Reaching a summit makes a climber light-headed, though no doctor is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not needing' removes M and B from MOUNTAIN CLIMB before 'dizzy' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A culmination is the highest point or climax of something.

clue.text: Variety list selected for it?

indicators.note: selected suggests the letters are picked out and arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A range of options picked out to suit something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'selected' rearranges the letters of VARIETY LIST, and the whole clue also describes the answer: a list chosen for its range.
explanation.definitionFit: Versatility is adaptability or the capacity for wide variety.

clue.text: Told it could be altered

indicators.note: could be means the letters of the word altered may form something else

explanation.surface: Someone is informed that a thing is open to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' signals an anagram of ALTERED; 'altered' itself looks like the anagram signal but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or recount it.

clue.text: Went ahead from the rear then appears to have been dragged through hedge backwards

parts.note: the rump is the rear end or buttocks
led means went in front

explanation.surface: A runner surges from the back of the field and finishes looking dishevelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' does not signal a reversal; it is part of the idiom for looking untidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone 'dragged through a hedge backwards' looks creased and untidy in British idiom.

clue.text: It's not a good thing to be raised in barren surroundings

indicators.note: in means the turned word is placed within the word for barren

parts.note: dry land is barren and unproductive

indicators.note: raised, in a down clue, means the word is read upwards from bottom to top

parts.note: to live is to exist, to be

explanation.surface: Growing up in a bleak environment is bad for a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' looks like upbringing, but in this down light it turns the word for 'to be' upward; 'in' sets that inside the word for barren, with 'surroundings' adding to the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilry is wicked mischief, hardly a virtuous matter.

clue.text: The womb, you said, certain to retract in time

indicators.note: in time means the abbreviation for time is put inside the rest
said means a word spoken aloud gives a letter of the same sound

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U

indicators.note: to retract means to draw back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone describes the womb, insisting their word will be withdrawn in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives the letter that sounds like 'you'; 'to retract' turns the word for certain backwards; 'in' then slips the time abbreviation in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The uterus is the anatomical organ in which a foetus grows.

clue.text: System used in some tricky calculations

indicators.note: used in means the letters run inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A method applied in complicated sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' tucks the answer inside 'some tricky'.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric system is the decimal scheme of measurement based on metres and grams.

clue.text: Pinches girl having fitting inside

indicators.note: inside means the word for suitable sits within the word for girl

parts.note: miss is a young woman or girl
appropriate means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A girl gets squeezed while being fitted for a dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinches' wants to be a dressmaker's squeeze; it is slang for steals.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is to steal, and to misappropriate is to take dishonestly.

clue.text: Catch the girl down below

parts.note: to net is to catch
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: Grab the young woman at the lower level.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or beneath, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: The girl turns up with remains of yesterday's dinner?

indicators.note: turns up, in a down clue, means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: her refers to a girl
ash is the remains of a fire

explanation.surface: A woman arrives with leftovers from the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' looks like arrives but turns HER upward to REH. The definition is playful: a rehash is old material served again, like reheated leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehash is old material reworked and served up again, like warmed-over food.

clue.text: With wintry conditions on return trip, skipper skirts old city

indicators.note: a return trip goes back the way it came, so the assembled letters read backwards
skirts means goes round the edge, so the skipper's word wraps round the city

parts.note: a lamb skips about in the fields
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A captain sails around an ancient port on his voyage home in wintry weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipper' wants to be a ship's captain; it is a young sheep that skips. 'skirts' wraps it round the ancient city, and 'on return trip' reads the whole thing backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Brumal is a literary adjective meaning of winter, wintry.

clue.text: Expressions of disgust about the endless marketing equipment

indicators.note: about means the jeers go round the shortened word

parts.note: boos are jeers expressing disgust

indicators.note: endless means the word the loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Jeers greet the never-ending sales kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last letter from 'the', and 'about' sets the two letters left inside the jeers.
explanation.definitionFit: Booths are stalls set up for selling goods at markets and fairs.

clue.text: First diner gets bad oyster it's said to kill!

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of diner is used
bad suggests the letters of oyster have gone off into a new order

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer is warned that a dodgy shellfish could be lethal.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the first of 'diner', joins ESTROY, the anagram of OYSTER signalled by 'bad'; 'it's said' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy is to wipe out or put to death.

clue.text: Charge for the ring

definitions.meaning: a payment levied, as at a bridge
to sound a bell with slow strokes

explanation.surface: The fee paid for a piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll is a fee for using a road or bridge, and to toll is to ring a bell slowly.

clue.text: Fashion in force

explanation.surface: Something that is in vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: To make is both to fashion an object and to compel someone, as in 'make him go'.

clue.text: Drink which is right for the liver?

definitions.meaning: an alcoholic beverage brewed from malt and hops
read as one who lives, a liver is someone who exists

explanation.surface: Asks which alcoholic beverage is good for the body's organ.
explanation.walkthrough: The liver seems to be the organ; read cryptically it is one who lives, i.e. one who is, so a be-er.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is a malted brew, and a 'be-er', one who exists, is a liver in the sense of someone living.

clue.text: They try to involve one in stratagems

indicators.note: in means the numeral letter goes inside the word stratagems
involve, in its old sense of coil up or entangle, says the letters are twisted together

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Schemers try to draw an individual into their plots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They try' looks like effort; it means hearing cases. 'in' puts I into STRATAGEMS and 'involve' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Magistrates hear and judge cases in the lower courts.

clue.text: Promise to ring a hospital in time

indicators.note: in time means the abbreviation for time is placed within the other letters

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A pledge to telephone a hospital promptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like telephone, but it is the round letter O; T then goes inside OAH.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn vow or sworn pledge.

clue.text: Here speaks a revolutionary playwright

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests the letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: Introducing a radical dramatist taking the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' seems to describe the playwright but signals an anagram of HERE SPEAKS A.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare is England's most celebrated dramatist.
